description: Deliver the private versioned External Agent API with grant-aware PAT authentication, durable idempotency, public execution projections, Session replay, and fenced Turn-stop behavior.

tasks.title: Add External Agent grants and bearer authorization
tasks.description: Add additive persistence for External Agent grants, keeping integration credentials and their existing ProjectId semantics separate. Extend PAT issuance, listing, revocation, CLI options, Bearer-only request resolution, and Project/scope authorization so an ExternalAgentCaller is resolved and authorized before resource lookup, body admission, or request-ledger access.
acceptanceCriteria: A PAT has exactly one valid External Agent grant form: a non-empty explicit Project set or operator_all; operator_all is rejected unless the PAT has operator scope, and readonly operator_all issuance is rejected before persistence. operator_all is evaluated at request time against a deployment-owned catalog containing only current private Projects, so removal or a non-private or non-owned transition denies access immediately.

Repeated --project bindings and --all-projects are supported by the server and CLI, are mutually exclusive, validate every canonical Project against the current authorization catalog before persistence, and leave no Credential or grant row after an unknown, non-private, non-owned, or otherwise failed binding.

The full PAT value is returned only by a successful create operation, is stored only as a hash, and list, audit, and revoke responses expose only safe metadata and the token prefix; revocation makes later direct authentication fail immediately.

The /api/v1 authentication branch accepts exactly one valid Authorization: Bearer PAT credential, rejects cookies, query-string tokens, Agent Connection identities, Runner credentials, malformed credentials, and revoked or expired PATs with the same safe 401 challenge behavior.

Grant and route-scope checks run before Project or canonical resource lookup and before request-body parsing for admission or mapping reads; an out-of-grant Project returns 403 without revealing whether the Project or mapping exists, while an authorized missing resource reaches the appropriate 404 path.

Server and CLI tests cover grant validation, atomic failure, operator_all catalog changes, explicit binding rejection, token disclosure, revocation, bearer rejection, scope enforcement, and authorization ordering using fake persistence and injectable time; the affected suites pass via npm run test:fast.
tasks.output: External Agent grant rows and migration, grant-aware PAT server/CLI lifecycle, ExternalAgentCaller resolution, bearer authorization middleware/service, and passing authentication tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design decisions 2 and 3. Do not reuse Credential.ProjectId or encode the grant in ScopesJson; existing Web, CLI, Agent Connection, Runner, and internal Session authentication behavior remains unchanged.

tasks.title: Build the durable external idempotency ledger
tasks.description: Add the ExternalAgentRequestMapping persistence model, unique indexes, and store, then implement the shared command-admission service for key validation, versioned server-computed fingerprints, caller/resource isolation, atomic claim, and durable outcome reconciliation. The service must preserve definitive rejection and unresolved unknown decisions and expose stable conflict results without returning raw requests or fingerprints.
acceptanceCriteria: Every write admission rejects a missing, duplicated, malformed, non-ASCII, or out-of-bounds Idempotency-Key with the specified safe 400 code before creating a mapping or any canonical or external effect.

The fingerprint includes the contract version, command kind, canonical route IDs, canonical scope, and the parsed text exactly as supplied; surrounding whitespace remains significant and follow-up ownership is derived from the canonical Session rather than the body.

Mappings are uniquely isolated by caller credential identity and command scope: launch by caller, Project, Agent, and key; follow-up by caller, Session, and key; stop by caller, Project, Session, Turn, and key.

The first request claims a durable mapping and stable reconciliation identity before invoking a canonical effect; a matching retry returns the original mapping and outcome without minting another Job, Input, Turn, dispatch, stop operation, or external effect.
A changed fingerprint returns stable 409 idempotency_key_reused, and key reuse by another caller or canonical resource creates an independent mapping rather than resolving an unrelated operation.

Definitive admission rejection is persisted as a terminal decision and returned unchanged on matching retries; an unresolved outcome remains queryable as unknown and polling or reconnecting never creates replacement work.

Ledger tests cover atomic claim races, response-loss recovery, conflicting payloads, caller/resource isolation, durable rejection, unknown recovery, and injectable TimeProvider behavior with fake canonical effect invokers; the affected server suites pass via npm run test:fast.
tasks.output: ExternalAgentRequestMapping schema and migration, shared command-admission/reconciliation service, and passing idempotency tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design decision 4. The ledger is the public retry boundary; existing launch-coordinator and Session-grain fences remain canonical execution authorities.

tasks.title: Build the public execution projection and journal engine
tasks.description: Add additive persistence for typed ExternalAgentProjectionSourceFact records, the allowlisted public execution snapshot, public Session event rows, source checkpoints, stream generations, sequence metadata, and retention state. Add the canonical producer mappings and implement the projector and reducer over those durable source facts so snapshots and public events commit transactionally, deduplicate source transitions, apply the five-state precedence rules, and expose a projection watermark for lag-aware API reads.
acceptanceCriteria: Every PublicExecutionRead contains all specified public keys with observedAt always present, null IDs only for absent canonical facts, and output/error limited to persisted safe public data; prompts, transcripts, Runtime or Runner identities, workspace paths, operation/fence IDs, provider payloads, and stack traces never serialize.

The reducer produces only accepted, queued, running, terminal, or unknown and covers prepared Job anchors, retryable capacity blocking, outcome_pending, durable rejection, unresolved effects, and terminal precedence without replaying unknown work.

Canonical producers append typed source facts in the same aggregate transaction as public-affecting launch, follow-up, capacity, Runner/result, stop-fence, and context-boundary mutations. The source inventory maps job.prepared, input.accepted, input.rejected, turn.queued, turn.running, turn.outcome_pending, turn.terminal, session.unknown, and durable session.context_reset facts without inferring ordered transitions from snapshots or raw AgentSessionEvents; incomplete historical source history is not exposed in the first release.

A prepared launch is addressable through its Job anchor with status=accepted and null Session, Input, and Turn IDs until canonical Session acceptance is projected; later canonical facts join the same public record rather than creating a second anchor.

The projector commits the public snapshot, normalized event identity, event sequence, stream generation/checkpoint, and source watermark in one transaction; crash-before-commit recovery leaves no partial state and replay-after-commit creates no duplicate sequence.

Public event filtering emits only input.accepted, input.rejected, turn.queued, turn.running, turn.outcome_pending, turn.terminal, session.unknown, or the separately constrained session.context_reset event, and emits session.context_reset only for a durable canonical context boundary; raw internal CloudEvents, transcript entries, AgentSessionEvents payloads, and UI/SignalR delivery are never used as the public journal.

A required source watermark ahead of the committed projection is observable as projection lag for API adapters, without converting the stale read to unknown; retention metadata preserves public events independently of transcript compaction.

Projection tests cover all five states, privacy allowlists, prepared-job anchoring, every typed source mapping including durable context reset and unresolved unknown, terminal precedence, incomplete-history rejection, transaction crash/replay behavior, deduplication, and projection-watermark lag using fake canonical facts, outboxes, and injectable TimeProvider; the affected server suites pass via npm run test:fast.
tasks.output: Public snapshot/event/checkpoint persistence and migration, canonical-fact projector/reducer, safe public mappers, and passing projection tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design decision 5 and the projection portion of the migration plan. Keep this projection separate from AgentSessionEvents, internal transcripts, Runner events, and UI event delivery; the worker must support disabled/observe-only rollout.

tasks.title: Expose launch, follow-up, and public resource reads
tasks.description: Implement the versioned /api/v1 route group for launch, Session input, Job read, Input read, and Turn read. Route each request through the shared authentication/grant and canonical ownership pipeline, strict JSON/header validation, idempotency reconciliation, canonical IAgentLauncher/AgentSession admission, projection checkpoint waiting, and dedicated public DTO mapping without serializing internal response types.
acceptanceCriteria: The API exposes POST /projects/{projectId}/agents/{agentId}/launch, POST /projects/{projectId}/agent-sessions/{sessionId}/inputs, GET agent-jobs/{jobId}, GET agent-inputs/{inputId}, and GET agent-turns/{turnId} under /api/v1 with operator scope for writes and readonly or operator scope for reads.

Launch and follow-up bodies accept only one required non-empty text string in a JSON object; unknown fields, duplicate property names, invalid JSON, attachments, context references, execution selectors, malformed headers, and caller-supplied ownership values return 400 before admission, while input text never appears in a response or public event.

A successful launch converges on at most one canonical AgentJob and initial Session/Input/Turn, remains readable by Job ID while Session acceptance is pending, and a follow-up appends to the canonical Session without creating another Job.

Each command and resource read returns the dedicated public object with every allowlisted field present and the correct five-state status, job/session/input/turn statuses, timestamps, outcome, safe reason, output, error, and sequence; internal DTOs and forbidden identities/details are absent.

The authorization order is observable in route tests: out-of-grant Projects return 403 before body parsing or mapping lookup, readonly callers cannot create any write state, and an authorized missing canonical resource returns 404 rather than public unknown.

Matching launch and follow-up retries return the original canonical identities and latest projection, changed keys return 409 idempotency_key_reused, durable admission rejection returns 200 terminal/rejected, and required projection lag returns 503 projection_lag without a new effect.

Route integration/spec tests cover the full launch-to-follow-up flow, prepared Job reads, strict validation, authorization ordering, all public statuses, response-loss replay, conflicting keys, projection lag, and privacy; the affected server suites pass via npm run test:fast.
tasks.output: Versioned launch/follow-up/Job/Input/Turn route handlers, public request/response contracts, canonical adapters, and passing direct API execution tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design decisions 1 and 3 for the non-event, non-stop routes. Preserve the existing /api/projects and internal Session route adapters unchanged.

tasks.title: Add durable Session event replay with opaque cursors
tasks.description: Add the /api/v1 Session-events read route over the public journal and implement the exact public page envelope, exact event allowlist, versioned cursor codec, exclusive pagination, stream-generation validation, retention floors, and closed-stream tombstones. Bind every cursor and read to the authorized Project and Session and expose only ordered public events and safe sequence bounds.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/agent-sessions/{sessionId}/events returns exactly the public page envelope sessionId, events, nextCursor, and highWaterSequence for only that authorized Session; each event has ascending sequence, opaque cursor, type, occurrence timestamp, and an allowlisted execution observation or constrained context-reset payload.

Replay emits only the seven execution event types input.accepted, input.rejected, turn.queued, turn.running, turn.outcome_pending, turn.terminal, and session.unknown, plus the separately constrained session.context_reset type; no other internal, transcript, CloudEvent, Runner, or UI event type is observable.

The default event limit is 100 and the maximum is 100; after is exclusive, nextCursor advances after the last returned event, and an empty page advances to the current high-water sequence without fabricating an event.

Cursors are versioned, tamper-evident, and bound to Project, Session, stream generation, and exclusive sequence position; malformed, cross-scope, tampered, or old-generation cursors return 400 cursor_invalid without falling back to the beginning.

A cursor before the retained floor returns 410 cursor_expired with only safe earliest/latest sequence bounds, and a closed Session retains a tombstone for the configured window while a no-cursor read returns 404 session_not_found.

Repeated and concurrent page reads remain ascending and stable by (SessionId, sequence), tolerate lost responses and out-of-order delivery, and never renumber or imply a missing event. A projector rebuild may create a new stream generation and invalidate old cursors, but nextSequence continues above the prior high-water sequence and never reuses or renumbers an identity; the stream remains available through transcript compaction and independent of SignalR or CloudEvent dispatch flags.
A canonical fact ahead of the public checkpoint returns 503 projection_lag, and a non-durable reset observation never creates a session.context_reset event.

Replay tests cover the exact page envelope, exact event allowlist and forbidden event types, reconnect/exclusive resume, empty high-water pages, default/max limits, cursor tampering and scope binding, generation changes with sequence continuity, retention expiry, closed tombstones, concurrent/repeated reads, projection lag, and context-reset privacy; the affected server suites pass via npm run test:fast.
tasks.output: Session event route, versioned cursor codec, retention/generation/tombstone handling, and passing replay tests.
tasks.notes: Completes the external-agent-session-replay capability on top of T-003's transactional journal. Cursors remain server-owned opaque values; handlers never accept a caller-decoded sequence.

tasks.title: Fence Turn-stop effects and terminal races
tasks.description: Implement the versioned Turn-stop route and public stop adapter through the existing Session/Runner control authority. Before any control effect, freeze the target revision, context generation, complete or explicit-null binding, and deadline in the caller-scoped mapping, then converge stop and execution results through one durable terminal fence and the public projection reducer.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/agent-turns/{turnId}/stop requires operator scope and exactly one valid Idempotency-Key, accepts an empty body only, verifies Project/Turn ownership before target selection, and exposes no Runner, Runtime, workspace, binding, operation, or provider identity.

The first stop persists the canonical Turn revision, context generation, binding choice, and deadline before issuing the existing control effect; a matching retry uses the frozen target and never contacts the Runner or creates a second stop effect.

A changed stop fingerprint returns 409 idempotency_key_reused, while a different key for a Turn with an unresolved stop returns 409 stop_outcome_unknown, leaves admission blocked, and cannot supersede or replay the unresolved effect.

A confirmed stop returns the original public Turn observation on response-loss retry, an unresolved stop remains public unknown and queryable through its original mapping, and polling or reconnecting never auto-replays it.

The terminal fence gives the first durable terminal fact precedence: a late Runner result or delayed projector delivery cannot rewrite public outcome, output, error, or event sequence, and at most one terminal public event remains.

Stop integration/spec tests cover empty-body and authorization ordering, target freezing, response-loss replay, changed-key conflict, unresolved stop, terminal/stop race ordering, late-result suppression, safe public mapping, and injectable deadline time; the affected server suites pass via npm run test:fast.
tasks.output: Versioned Turn-stop route, caller-scoped frozen stop mapping, terminal-fence integration with canonical control and projection, and passing stop-race tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design decision 6. Reuse the existing Session/Runner control path and keep unresolved external effects observable rather than automatically replayed.

tasks.title: Enable and publish the complete External Agent contract
tasks.description: Wire the feature-flagged rollout guard across grant issuance and /api/v1 admissions, add readiness/checkpoint handling for newly created Sessions with complete typed source history, explicitly keep pre-contract historical Sessions out of the first release, and publish the exact shipped contract in docs/auth.md, docs/agent-api.md, and implementation-status guidance. Add cross-capability integration coverage that exercises the public lifecycle without introducing a second execution path.
acceptanceCriteria: The direct API and new External Agent grant issuance remain disabled until the configured projection readiness/checkpoint condition is met. First-release readiness admits only newly created Sessions with complete typed source history; a known pre-contract or incomplete Session returns 503 projection_lag with a safe projection-unavailable reason rather than 404, an empty stream, or fabricated events. Pausing or resuming the projector preserves durable mappings and checkpoints without replaying unresolved effects.

docs/auth.md documents Bearer PATs, explicit Project and operator_all grants, scopes, issuance/list/revoke disclosure rules, and authorization ordering; docs/agent-api.md documents every /api/v1 route, required keys/bodies, public fields/states, errors, cursor semantics, lag behavior, and stop fencing without exposing internal identities.

Implementation-status guidance distinguishes the shipped public contract from existing Web, CLI, Agent Connection, Runner, and internal Session adapters and records the selected retention, cursor-key, no-first-release-historical-backfill, and public-output policies required to enable the route.

Cross-capability integration tests create a granted PAT, launch once, recover a lost response with the same key, follow up on the returned Session, resume events with an exclusive cursor, read public resources, and stop a Turn while asserting no duplicate canonical records or forbidden fields.

Integration coverage verifies unauthorized and readonly behavior, conflicting keys, durable rejection, projection lag for an ineligible historical Session and a source watermark ahead of a newly eligible Session, cursor expiry, stop/terminal races, and existing internal route regression behavior using only fakes and injectable TimeProvider.
Additive migrations apply cleanly, the complete affected server/CLI test set passes, and npm run verify succeeds.
tasks.output: Feature-flagged External Agent rollout wiring, published auth/API/status documentation, cross-capability integration coverage, and a passing full verification gate.
tasks.notes: Completes the migration plan's rollout and documentation steps. Enabling production access must preserve the additive rollback rule: disable new admissions and grants without deleting mappings, projection data, or canonical work.
